subject: Banks Silently Changed These Rewards on This Credit Card
summary: ICICI drops its lounge-access spend threshold, HSBC adds a capped Amazon offer, and Equitas opens a 1:1 voucher redemption.
body_html:
Nobody calls you when your credit card changes. No email, no push notification that actually explains anything, no "hey, we just rewrote how your lounge access works." Banks update a line on a webpage, and unless you happen to be reading their T&Cs for fun on a Tuesday — which, let's be honest, nobody is — you find out the hard way. At the airport. At the redemption screen. Three months from now, when the math doesn't add up the way it used to.

I track these changes as they happen, straight from the banks' own pages. Here's what actually moved today — not the marketing spin, just the before and after, and what it means for your wallet.

ICICI Emirates Emeralde: your domestic lounge access just got easier (for once, a change in your favour)

Here's the old rule, buried in the fine print: to get domestic lounge access on the ICICI Bank Emirates Emeralde Credit Card, you had to spend ₹75,000 or more in a quarter — and even then, you didn't get the benefit right away. It kicked in the following quarter. So if you had a slow spending quarter, you paid for lounge access with your card fee and got nothing for it.

That condition is gone. As of today, ICICI has rewritten this: primary cardholders get unlimited complimentary domestic lounge access, no spend threshold, no quarter-long wait. You swipe the card, you walk in.

Let's do the math on what that was actually costing you. If your spending dipped below ₹75,000 in even one quarter a year, you lost lounge access for the next three months — while still paying the card's annual fee. For someone who travels for work but has an uneven spend pattern (a slow month here, a heavy one there), this single change could be worth several lounge visits a year that you'd have otherwise paid ₹1,000-plus each for, out of pocket.

The catch: this is domestic lounge access specifically. International lounge access through Priority Pass still runs on its own terms — check the current criteria before you assume it's unlimited too, because ICICI didn't touch that clause today.

If you're an existing Emeralde cardholder, this is one of the rare cases where a silent change actually helps you. You don't need to do anything — it's live already.

HSBC Taj Credit Card: a new Amazon offer just landed

HSBC added a fresh deal to the Taj Credit Card today — 20% off at Amazon, capped at ₹5,000, when you spend ₹10,000 or more in a single month.

Run the number before you get excited: to earn the full ₹5,000 cap, you'd need to spend ₹25,000 in that month (20% of ₹25,000 is ₹5,000). If your typical Amazon spend is closer to ₹10,000–15,000, you're looking at ₹2,000–3,000 back, not the headline ₹5,000. Read that as "up to," not "guaranteed."

The catch that always comes with these month-gated offers: it's a use-it-or-lose-it window. Miss the ₹10,000 threshold in a given month and you get nothing that month — no rollover, no averaging. If your Amazon spending is lumpy (a big order in November for Diwali, nothing in February), this offer rewards you unevenly. Worth checking the T&Cs PDF on HSBC's page for the exact redemption mechanics and exclusions — categories like gift cards and certain top-up products are usually carved out of offers like this.

If you already shop on Amazon regularly and can hit ₹10,000 most months, this is free money sitting on a card you already carry. If you don't, don't let the 20% headline pull your spending toward Amazon just to chase it — that's the offer working on you, not for you.

Equitas Powermiles: reward points can now convert 1:1 into real vouchers

The Equitas Small Finance Bank Powermiles Credit Card added a new redemption route today: your accumulated reward points can now be burned at a 1:1 rate for e-gift vouchers from five brands — Apple, Tanishq, Taj Hotels, Marks & Spencer, and The Body Shop.

Why this matters more than it sounds: a lot of reward point programs quietly redeem at a worse rate when you cash out — you'll see 1 point = ₹0.25 or ₹0.50 buried in the redemption catalogue, which effectively cuts your earned rewards in half before you've spent a rupee of them. A genuine 1:1 burn rate against real brand vouchers is the exception, not the rule, and it's worth checking your own points balance today to see what that's actually worth in your pocket.

The catch: it's limited to five brands. If none of these are where you'd naturally spend a voucher, the "1:1" headline doesn't help you — you're choosing between a good exchange rate on a store you don't shop at, or a worse rate somewhere you'd actually use. Before you redeem, check whether Tanishq or Taj Hotels (the two higher-value ones on this list) line up with anything you're already planning to buy — a piece of jewellery, a hotel stay. That's where this update is genuinely worth acting on, not just noting.

What I'd actually do with this

If you hold the ICICI Emirates Emeralde card, this is a straightforward win — no action needed, just know your domestic lounge access no longer depends on last quarter's spending. If you're on the HSBC Taj card, this offer is only worth chasing if ₹10,000+ Amazon spend is already your normal month — don't inflate your spending to catch a ₹5,000 cap you were never going to hit. And if you're sitting on Equitas Powermiles points, go check your balance today — a genuine 1:1 redemption against Tanishq or Taj Hotels is worth using before it changes again, because these terms move quietly, and you just saw how quietly.

This is my honest read of what changed today, not formal financial advice — I track these updates as they happen, but you know your own spending better than any newsletter does. Before you make a big call based on any of this, check the bank's current T&Cs directly; terms like these can shift again tomorrow, silently, the same way they did today.

— Monzy

New offer: 20% off at Amazon, capped at ₹5,000, on ₹10,000 or more spent in a single month.
